bug_info.bug_desc: In Standard speed mode, sd_en_o[0] was unconditionally assigned 1'b1 whenever any chip select was active. This enabled the SPI data output driver even during receive-only and dummy segments, causing the host to drive the shared data line with stale shift-register data when the spec requires all data output drivers to be disabled for receive-only and dummy segments. Additionally, simply replacing the constant with cmd_wr_en_q could deassert the output enable early at the end of the final transmitted byte, because cmd_wr_en_q may change up to half a serial-clock period before the bit/sample period ends depending on cpol/cpha. The fix gates the Standard-mode output enable with cmd_wr_en_q and stretches it through the end of the final bit period using a dedicated last-bit enable register.
bug_info.fix_hint: In spi_host_fsm.sv, gate sd_en_o[0] in Standard mode by the transmit-byte enable (cmd_wr_en_q) instead of tying it high. Add a register (cmd_wr_en_last_bit) that is set when cmd_wr_en_q is active during the last bit period and cleared at byte_ending, then use cmd_wr_en_q | cmd_wr_en_last_bit for sd_en_o[0]. This keeps the output driver disabled for receive-only/dummy segments while ensuring it remains asserted through the final bit period of a transmit-capable segment.
